mappings.note: A meristem subtype is named from the growth it produces (girth, wood), which is the role-of-tissues outcome. LO-1 deliberately not cited: apical/lateral/intercalary is not one of the discriminations LO-1 lists, and the item never asks meristematic vs permanent.

The false statement is a role claim (vertical root growth), and the two true ones are position plus regeneration after grazing, so what is scored is what intercalary meristem does for the plant. Same outcome as the lateral-meristem item, different tissue and different false lure.

Two micrographs, and the discriminator asked for is a wall feature - pectin-thickened corners vs lignified dead walls. That is the collenchyma/sclerenchyma line named in LO-1, read off structure, hence C-4.2-LO-2 alongside.

LO-6 names this experiment: root elongation stops when the terminal tip is cut, so the dividing cells are apical. C-8.2-LO-2 because the conclusion must be drawn from a five-day length table rather than recalled.

Both assertion and reason are about a cell feature (absence of large vacuoles) and why that feature suits continuous division - structure related to function. No tissue is being told apart, so LO-1 is not cited.

The pillar-like (columnar) shape must be connected to surface area for absorption, so structure-to-function leads; C3.2 second because the life process served is nutrition/absorption in animals. Paired with the thin-epithelium item in part 1, which serves exchange of materials instead.
Ordering cell-tissue-organ-organ system-organism is the level-of-organisation outcome verbatim. Nothing about any individual tissue's structure or role is scored.

Names the process that converts dividing cells into permanent tissue, i.e. the meristematic/permanent boundary LO-1 is built on. Fit is fair rather than exact - the frame has no outcome about differentiation as a process in its own right.

A negative-stem item where every option is a cell feature and the student must know which features enable division. Purely structure-to-function; the sclerenchyma comparison appears only in the rationale, not the task.

The statement that has to be rejected is a role claim (that epidermis conducts water), so role-of-tissues leads; C-4.2-LO-2 for the two true statements, which are the single-layer packing and cuticle secretion.

One-mark recall of a structure's name and what it does. Kept to the role outcome alone; C3.2 is reserved for items where the exchange or transport process itself has to be reasoned about, as in the no-stomata item in part 1.

Single structural adaptation (thick cutin) matched to a single functional demand (water conservation). Narrower than the desert-vs-underwater item in part 1, which also needed the epidermal role, so C-4.2-LO-3 is not cited here.
A four-way match across parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma and epidermis - the explicit discrimination in LO-1 - keyed on structural features, hence C-4.2-LO-2.
Identify-the-tissue from a characteristics list, with the other simple permanent tissues as distractors. The features are given, so nothing has to be derived from structure; LO-1 alone.

Tendon-to-bone force transmission and ligament stabilisation are the roles of two connective tissues in an animal. C-5.3-LO-2 withheld by rule: it is used only where the stem frames physical activity or fitness, and this is a labelled anatomical diagram.
Aerenchyma is identified from the service it provides an aquatic plant (buoyancy), not from any structural description in the stem - role of tissues.

Single-step attribution of flexibility to collenchyma, with no explanation of the wall thickening required. Split from the coriander/coconut items in part 1, which demand the structural reason (C-4.2-LO-2) or the sclerenchyma contrast (LO-1).
The reason offered is a structural one (dead cells, thick lignified walls) and the student must judge whether it explains the observed toughness. Textbook structure-to-function.

Three tissues identified from a wall-nature and intercellular-space table, which is the parenchyma/collenchyma/sclerenchyma discrimination driven off structure. Not C-8.2-LO-2 - the table is a presentation device, not data to be interpreted.
Asks what defines a complex permanent tissue against simple ones - the simple/complex clause of LO-1 - and nothing about any particular tissue's function.
The whole item rests on knowing sieve tubes are phloem, not xylem: a xylem/phloem discrimination, named in LO-1.

Picks the one component of a complex tissue that carries a named function (living, stores reserve food). This is within-xylem role assignment, not the xylem/phloem line, so LO-1 is not cited here although the neighbouring item does.
Classification of the elbow against the joint-type list in LO-1. Anatomy only; no fitness or movement-quality reasoning, so C-5.3-LO-2 stays out.

Sequencing the steps of a named investigation is the inquiry competency C8.2. C7.1 second because cellular totipotency and tissue culture are the frontier-science content in this chapter; LO-5, the only outcome under C7.1, is about muscular injury and does not fit.
The stem says 'unlike the xylem' outright, so the scored act is the living-vs-dead contrast between phloem and xylem - the xylem/phloem discrimination in LO-1.
